data.narrative:
Marathon Fusion is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Adam Rutkowski and Kyle Schiller, seeking valuation after raising $10.9M to date. The nuclear energy sector comprises 11 comparable firms: three public entities (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private-stage companies including Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

The peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy peer set; only one seed-stage peer and one adjacent-stage peer were identified, below the three-datapoint threshold needed for reliability. Stage-progression methodology proved more defensible. Using the $10.9M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields $27.3M.

The triangulated analysis supports a median valuation of $27M, with a 15% confidence range bounded by $23M (low) and $31M (high). This single-method result carries material execution risk; valuation hinges on the appropriateness of the 2.5x step-up assumption and the representativeness of capital raised as a proxy for current value. Key uncertainties include technology maturity, regulatory pathway clarity, and burn rate relative to the $10.9M capitalization. A broader peer dataset or revenue-based metrics would strengthen conviction, currently limited by the nascent stage and sector specificity of Marathon Fusion's comparables.
